query: For the paper "LibriVoxDeEn: A Corpus for German-to-English Speech Translation and German Speech Recognition" (arXiv: 1910.07924), answer this question: How is the speech alignment quality evaluated?

drafts: Speech (audio-text) alignment quality is evaluated through a manual evaluation using a 3-point scale: 1) wrong alignment, 2) partial alignment (some words or sentences may be missing), and 3) correct alignment, allowing non-spoken syllables at the start or end [1]. Two annotators each rated 30 items from each bin, with 10 items shared between them to enable measuring inter-annotator reliability [1]. Inter-annotator agreement was measured using Krippendorff's α-reliability score for ordinal ratings, which reached 1.00 for audio-text alignment quality ratings [8]. The results were averaged over 90 items and two raters [7], and the audio-text alignment was rated as being of generally high quality [9].

The inter-annotator agreement between two raters was measured by Krippendorff’s α-reliability score (Krippendorff, 2013) for ordinal ratings. The inter- annotator reliability for text-to-text alignment quality ratings scored 0.77, while for audio-text alignment quality ratings it scored 1.00.
The audio-text alignment was rated as in general as high qual- ity.
